title: Rational-point transport and its scheme-Frobenius normalization
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in a fixed algebraic closure. Let $X_0$ be separated of finite type over $k_0$, put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$ and $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, and write $g_X=\operatorname{id}_{X_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$ and $g_s=\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$ for geometric Frobenius [def-weil-frobenius-detailed]. Fix $m\geq1$ and $y\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})$ with induced geometric point $\bar y:s\to X$. For $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ ($n\geq1$), $\mathcal O_E$ or $E$, use the finite, derived-complete integral, or rationalized constructible category and its pullbacks [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Put $G_\Lambda=Lg_{X,\Lambda}^*$ and $J_{y,\Lambda}=\operatorname{Fib}_{s,\Lambda}L\bar y_\Lambda^*$, with point fiber functor [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point].

Throughout, specify the integral pullback-composition and pullback scalar comparison families by the strict-system realization formulas of [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization]; these are the choices of the comparison isomorphisms in [lem-pod-integral-pullback-composition] and [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension]. 

One has $g_X^m\bar y=\bar y g_s^m$. Define $t_{y,m,K}:J_{y,\Lambda}K\to J_{y,\Lambda}G_\Lambda^mK$ by the $m$ successive point transports of [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport] on $L\bar y^*K$, followed by the canonical pullback-composition identification for that equality (at integral level use [lem-pod-integral-pullback-composition], and rationalize at $E$). This is natural: for every morphism $u:K\to L$,
$$J_{y,\Lambda}(G_\Lambda^mu)t_{y,m,K}=t_{y,m,L}J_{y,\Lambda}(u).$$

At finite level let $\Phi$ be the $q$-power scheme Frobenius [def-trf-scheme-frobenius], let $\kappa^{(m)}:L(\Phi^m)^*\xrightarrow{\sim}L(g_X^m)^*$ be the specified multiplicative comparison of [prop-trf-scheme-galois-comparison], and let $\rho_{y,m,K}:J_{y,\Lambda}K\to J_{y,\Lambda}L(\Phi^m)^*K$ be the canonical pullback-composition identification from $\Phi^m\bar y=\bar y$. Under the identification $L(g_X^m)^*\cong G_\Lambda^m$, one has
$$t_{y,m,K}=J_{y,\Lambda}(\kappa^{(m)}_K)\rho_{y,m,K}.$$
Here $\kappa^{(m)}$ uses the canonical absolute-Frobenius trivialization, with no scalar rescaling. This equality commutes with quotient-coefficient transitions as an equality of the specified maps on simultaneous strict reduction systems. Its integral realization and rationalization give the same equality at the integral and rational stages. No finite Tor-amplitude hypothesis on reductions of an integral object is required.

For finite coefficient fields $E\subset M$, write $T=-\otimes_E M$, let $d_K:T G_E^mK\xrightarrow{\sim}G_M^mTK$ be the iterated canonical pullback comparison of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension], and let $b_K:J_{y,E}K\otimes_E M\xrightarrow{\sim}J_{y,M}TK$ be the pullback comparison followed by the point-sections comparison [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension]. Then
$$J_{y,M}(d_K)b_{G_E^mK}(t_{y,m,K}\otimes_E M)=t_{y,m,TK}b_K.$$
These are comparisons in the framework rationalized categories [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], with the same identity and tower identifications as the specified scalar comparisons.

proof.text: Write $g=g_X$, $h=g_s^m$, $H=\operatorname{Fr}^{(q^m)}_X$ and $r=\operatorname{Fr}^{(q^m)}_s=h^{-1}$. The last equality follows from the arithmetic/geometric inverse convention in [def-weil-frobenius-detailed]. By [thm-trf-frobenius-fixed-points], the $k$-point $\bar y$ obtained from the specified rational point satisfies $\Phi^m\bar y=\bar y$. The factorization [prop-trf-frobenius-factorization] and the inverse convention give $\Phi^m=g^mH$. Absolute Frobenius is natural: on affine rings this is the identity $f(a^{q^m})=f(a)^{q^m}$, so $H\bar y=\bar y r$. Therefore $g^m\bar y r=\bar y$, and composition with $h$ gives $g^m\bar y=\bar y h$. These are equalities of scheme maps; semilinear $g$ is not being treated as a $k$-morphism.

proof.text: Let $H_\Lambda=Lg_{s,\Lambda}^*$ and $P_\Lambda=L\bar y_\Lambda^*$. Define $I^{(0)}_N=1$ and $I^{(j+1)}_N=\iota_{H_\Lambda^jN}\,I^{(j)}_N$, so $I^{(m)}_N:\operatorname{Fib}_sN\to\operatorname{Fib}_sH_\Lambda^mN$. Each $\iota$ is the specified map of [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport]. By [lem-weil-frobenius-point-transport-natural](2), induction gives $\operatorname{Fib}_s(H_\Lambda^m v)I^{(m)}_N=I^{(m)}_{N'}\operatorname{Fib}_s(v)$ for every $v:N\to N'$: apply the one-step naturality equation to $H_\Lambda^jv$ and compose with the induction equation. The scheme equality in Step 1 gives a natural comparison $v_{\Lambda,K}:H_\Lambda^mP_\Lambda K\xrightarrow{\sim}P_\Lambda G_\Lambda^mK$ using [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] at finite level, [lem-pod-integral-pullback-composition] integrally, and their rationalizations. Put $t_{y,m,K}=\operatorname{Fib}_s(v_{\Lambda,K})I^{(m)}_{P_\Lambda K}$. Naturality of $v$ and the displayed induction equation give exactly $J_y(G_\Lambda^mu)t_{y,m,K}=t_{y,m,L}J_y(u)$.

proof.text: At finite coefficients the point calculation can be made on a sheaf $N$, then degreewise on a complex. By [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image](1), $(Lh^*N)(s)=N(s\xrightarrow{h}s)$. Under this identification, restriction followed by colimit insertion in [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport] is $\operatorname{res}_h:N(s,1)\to N(s,h)$; composing $m$ such maps is restriction along $h=g_s^m$. Let $\tau_s:Lr^*\to1$ be the canonical absolute-Frobenius trivialization specified by [lem-pur-frobenius-trivialization-pullback], with exponent $am$. At the final object its value on a sheaf $M$ is $(\operatorname{res}_r^M)^{-1}$: the relative-Frobenius identification in that statement, adjointed to inverse image and evaluated at the final object, is the inverse of restriction along the isomorphism $r:(s,r)\to(s,1)$. For $M=Lh^*N$, this restriction identifies with $\operatorname{res}_r:N(s,h)\to N(s,1)$; its inverse is $\operatorname{res}_h$. Thus under $Lr^*Lh^*N\cong N$ one has $\Gamma(s,\tau_{s,Lh^*N})=I_N^{(m)}$. Exact constant-coefficient pullback [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact] and exact point sections [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact] make this a degreewise identity computing the derived maps. No scalar is inserted.

source.place: Tag 0F6W, lemma-relative-frobenius-weakly-etale; final-object calculation with the specified adjoint trivialization

proof.text:
Expand the canonical comparison specified in the statement: with $\tau_X:LH^*\to1$, it is $\kappa_K^{(m)}=(\tau_X)_{L(g^m)^*K}\circ c_{H,g^m,K}$, where $c_{H,g^m}:L\Phi^{m*}\to LH^*L(g^m)^*$ is the canonical composition map. This is the cancellation of absolute Frobenius in $\Phi^m=g^mH$ from [prop-trf-scheme-galois-comparison], with its required canonical normalization. Apply the pullback-naturality equation of [lem-pur-frobenius-trivialization-pullback] to $u=\bar y$ and exponent $am$. It identifies $P_\Lambda(\tau_X)$ with $\tau_sP_\Lambda$ under $H\bar y=\bar y r$. Use [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] to identify the successive pullbacks. After precomposition with the fixed-point identification $\rho_{y,m,K}$, the resulting map is $\Gamma(s,\tau_{s,P_\Lambda L(g^m)^*K})$ with source identified with $P_\Lambda K$ through $Lr^*H_\Lambda^m\cong1$ and $v_{\Lambda,K}$. Naturality of $\tau_s$ with respect to $v_{\Lambda,K}$ and Step 3 give
$$J_{y,\Lambda}(\kappa_K^{(m)})\rho_{y,m,K}=\operatorname{Fib}_s(v_{\Lambda,K})I^{(m)}_{P_\Lambda K}=t_{y,m,K}.$$
Here the canonical composition identifications on the two paths agree: on a pullback of a section both send it to the same section on the iterated fiber product, with its same projections. The termwise description in the cited composition statement computes those identifications.

proof.text: The equality of Step 4 holds before localizing complexes. For an integral object choose one flat-term K-flat resolution $Q\to K$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] and use the simultaneous quotients $Q_n=Q\otimes(A_{E,n})_X$. They are K-flat with flat terms by [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings]. Every restriction used in Step 3, every colimit coprojection, and the relative-Frobenius isomorphisms specifying $\tau$ is a natural map of module sheaves, hence commutes with $Q_{n+1}\to Q_n$. The coefficient factors send a tensor $x\otimes b$ to the restriction of $x$ tensored with $b$; reduction before or after this map therefore gives the same tensor. The termwise pullback-composition maps of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] have the same property. Consequently Step 4 is an equality of maps of these strict quotient diagrams, including their transitions. For derived change of the finite coefficient ring, [lem-trf-scheme-galois-coefficient-change] gives the equation for the specified $\kappa^{(m)}$, with no flatness or Tor-amplitude assumption; the point comparison [lem-trf-point-sections-finite-reduction] applies because every reduction of an integral constructible object is bounded by [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]; it does not require a perfect complex. Thus the maps used here are compatible with both the strict transitions and their canonical derived coefficient identifications.

proof.text: For $N=P_{\mathcal O_E}K$, [lem-trf-integral-point-transport-tower-realization] identifies each specified integral $\iota_{H_{\mathcal O_E}^jN}$ with realization of the actual point-transport morphism of its coherent quotient tower. The formulas for $c$ and $\eta$ in [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization] identify the integral composition map itself with realization of the strict termwise composition maps, including the comparison from the realized iterated tower to the iterated completed pullback. Apply those formulas to the square $g^m\bar y=\bar y h$ and to each splitting into successive pullbacks. The strict left-hand map of Step 5 is the composite of these termwise composition maps and the finite point transports. Its realization is therefore exactly $\operatorname{Fib}_s(v_{\mathcal O_E,K})I^{(m)}_{P_{\mathcal O_E}K}$ of Step 2. The right-hand map realizes, by the same specified composition identifications, to the stipulated realization of $J_y(\kappa^{(m)})\rho$. Apply the functor $R\lim$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit] to the equality of whole strict maps from Step 5. This proves the integral equality. No step infers an integral equality solely from equal individual reductions, and no finite Tor-amplitude assumption enters.

proof.text: By [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] the objects at $E$ are the integral objects and their morphisms are $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_E}\otimes E$. By [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport] the rational point transport is the scalar extension of the integral transport. Applying rationalization to Step 6 gives the required normalization at $E$. For rational naturality it suffices to take a morphism $f\otimes\lambda$: both sides of the naturality equation of Step 2 become $\lambda$ times the rationalization of its integral equation for $f$, by the linear formulas for pullback in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] and for the point functor in [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. Additivity gives the equation for every morphism. Thus this argument covers morphisms in the raw framework rationalization and does not replace it by a larger category or invoke an idempotent completion.

proof.text:
Write $T_s$ for scalar extension on $s$, $a_K:T_sP_EK\to P_MTK$ for the pullback comparison, and $\delta_N:T_sH_E^mN\to H_M^mT_sN$ for the iterated point pullback comparison. The comparisons are now specified by [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization], not characterized by their individual reductions. Its composition/scalar equation, applied along the two equal scheme maps $g^m\bar y=\bar y g_s^m$, and then along every splitting of $g^m$ and $g_s^m$, gives
$$v_{M,TK}H_M^m(a_K)\delta_{P_EK}=P_M(d_K)a_{G_E^mK}T_s(v_{E,K}).$$
Indeed its left path first uses the scalar comparisons for the successive point pullbacks and for $\bar y$, and then the compositor defining $v_M$; its right path first uses $v_E$, then the scalar comparison for $\bar y$ and the successive $g$ pullbacks. The lemma's equation interchanges a scalar comparison with each compositor, and its equality-of-scheme-maps and associativity clauses identify the two paths. These are equalities of the specified simultaneous quotient-diagram maps and hence their integral realizations; the rationalization clause gives the displayed equation. The identity and coefficient-tower clauses use the completion-normalized tensor associator, matching that in [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension]. No assertion about the unaccepted proof of lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension is used.

proof.text:
Let $\beta_N:\operatorname{Fib}_{s,E}N\otimes_E M\to\operatorname{Fib}_{s,M}T_sN$ be the inverse of the rational sections comparison of [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension]. The scalar-compatibility clause of [lem-weil-frobenius-point-transport-natural](2) gives, for one step, $\operatorname{Fib}_{s,M}(\delta_N)\beta_{H_EN}(\iota_N\otimes M)=\iota_{T_sN}\beta_N$. Apply that equation in turn to $N,H_EN,\ldots,H_E^{m-1}N$; naturality of $\iota$ moves each intermediate pullback comparison across the next transport. The adjacent comparison factors compose to the iterated $\delta_N$, giving
$$\operatorname{Fib}_{s,M}(\delta_N)\beta_{H_E^mN}(I_N^{(m)}\otimes M)=I_{T_sN}^{(m)}\beta_N.$$
The point comparisons are exactly those of Step 8: the strict-system choices and their scalar associator are specified by [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization]. For identity and successive field extensions the equations use the identity and associator clauses of [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension] and [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension], so the same induction gives those compatibilities for every $m$.

proof.text:
By its definition in the statement, $b_K=\operatorname{Fib}_{s,M}(a_K)\beta_{P_EK}$. Expand $t_{y,m,K}=\operatorname{Fib}_{s,E}(v_{E,K})I^{(m)}_{P_EK}$ on the left-hand side of the desired coefficient equation. Naturality of $\beta$ with respect to $v_{E,K}$ rewrites it as
$$\operatorname{Fib}_{s,M}\!\left(P_M(d_K)a_{G_E^mK}T_s(v_{E,K})\right)\beta_{H_E^mP_EK}(I^{(m)}_{P_EK}\otimes M).$$
Substitute the square proved in Step 8 and the iterated point equation of Step 9. The result is
$$\operatorname{Fib}_{s,M}\!\left(v_{M,TK}H_M^m(a_K)\right)I^{(m)}_{T_sP_EK}\beta_{P_EK}.$$
Naturality of $I^{(m)}$ for $a_K$, proved in Step 2, makes this $\operatorname{Fib}_{s,M}(v_{M,TK})I^{(m)}_{P_MTK}\operatorname{Fib}_{s,M}(a_K)\beta_{P_EK}=t_{y,m,TK}b_K$. This proves the final displayed equation. The identity and tower identifications remain the specified ones because each substitution uses the same comparisons as Steps 8 and 9. The naturality of $\beta$ used here is part of [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension].

tool_uses.why: Step 1 takes the equality Phi^m ybar = ybar for the chosen rational point; the trace-transport unit does not itself state the fixed-point theorem.
Step 1 takes the factorization of scheme Frobenius into absolute and Galois Frobenius to prove g^m ybar = ybar g_s^m; no local factorization is supplied by this unit.
Steps 2 and 9 take naturality and the specified one-step scalar-compatibility equation for point transport; this unit only requires their transported iterates.
Steps 2, 4 and 5 take the canonical termwise finite module pullback compositor and its K-flat description; no such sheaf-functor construction belongs to the trace-transport unit.
Step 2 takes existence and naturality of integral pullback composition, with its choice specified by the new realization node; the trace unit provides no integral pullback construction.
Step 3 takes clause (1), evaluation of inverse image under a scheme isomorphism, to identify restriction along h; this is a generic site tool absent from the trace unit.
Steps 3 and 4 take the relative-Frobenius normalization and pullback-naturality of the canonical absolute-Frobenius trivialization; these finite site comparisons are not proved by the trace unit.
Step 3 takes exactness of constant-coefficient pullback, making the sheaf calculation compute derived maps; the trace unit supplies no exactness result for inverse image.
Step 3 takes exactness of sections at Spec of an algebraically closed field to pass the point restriction calculation to complexes; the trace unit does not prove this site fact.
Step 4 takes the specified canonical comparison kappa built by cancelling absolute Frobenius; the trace-transport unit uses rather than constructs this comparison.
Step 5 takes a flat-term K-flat resolution to form one simultaneous family of quotients; the trace unit provides no resolution existence theorem.
Step 5 takes preservation of flat-term K-flatness by coefficient change so all quotients compute derived reductions; the trace unit does not supply this resolution tool.
Step 5 takes compatibility of the actual kappa with derived finite coefficient change without a Tor-amplitude restriction; the trace unit requires but does not prove this finite comparison.
Step 5 takes point-sections compatibility with finite derived reduction for bounded-above complexes; the trace unit does not construct the point-reduction comparison.
Step 6 takes realization of the specified integral point transport from its whole coherent quotient tower; the trace unit does not identify that chain-level map.
Step 6 takes functorial R lim on strict tower complexes, preserving the equality of actual tower maps; the trace unit supplies no construction of this derived functor.

Step 9 takes the identity and field-tower clauses for the pullback scalar comparison; its particular pullback family is specified by the new realization node, and the trace unit has no coefficient-operation comparison theorem.
Steps 8, 9 and 10 take the specified sections comparison, its naturality and its completion-normalized field-tower associator; the trace unit requires these as generic coefficient tools.

lean.note: Successor indices cover every positive m and finite coefficient exponent. Normalization unfolds the finite, integral, rational, whole strict-system and scalar equations. Helper definitions give the prescribed canonical maps; chosen data are uniquely characterized, never arbitrary maps. Integral comparisons use IntegralComparisonSystem and its prescribed whole-system realization formulas. No Tor-amplitude hypothesis is introduced. Finite transport is recursively composed from frobeniusPointTransportFinite, the unit-normalized pointPowerPullbackModel and proEtaleConstantRingPullbackComposition; finiteOrdinary and StrictFormula use this same successive iterate. Compile-budget repair explicitly reuses the canonical point/scheme invertibility instances, with no extra hypotheses.
